findings.title: Stray sed backup file committed
findings.description: The diff adds `CoreServiceFactory.test.ts-E`, and a glob confirms it exists. It is a verbatim copy of the pre-change test file. The `-E` suffix is what BSD `sed -i -E` leaves behind on macOS, so it is a tooling artifact. The file is dead code. It also sits under `tests/`, so a broad test glob could pick it up. Delete it, and consider adding `*-E` to `.gitignore`.

findings.title: AdoptionError is swallowed or reported only through message text for non-ContextIntegrator callers
findings.description: `generateContextFromProject` rethrows `PermissivenessFragmentError` and `AdoptionError`. Every other error is logged and turned into an error-stub string that is returned as if it were valid context. That stub behavior predates this change. The new adoption path adds a second pass through the same catch, though. `persistInProgress` wraps write failures in `AdoptionError`, but the `readFile` and parse calls in `assertGuideSupportsAdoption`, `readHistory` and `measureSourceVolume` can throw plain errors. Those become a stub prompt instead of a failure. For a project that was meant to be adopted, that stub is a concept prompt, which is the misleading fallback the new comment says to avoid. The integration test at `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts:63` asserts that no stub is produced, but only for the happy paths. Consider wrapping unexpected I/O failures in the resolver as `AdoptionError`.

findings.title: Required `adoptionStateWrites` parameter is applied consistently
findings.description: Making the option required forces each caller to decide. All production callers are updated. `build.ts` and `context_build` use `persist`. `template_preview` and the tests that don't test adoption use `read-only`. A grep of `createContextPipeline(` found no caller left on the old signature.

findings.title: Resolver design and test coverage look sound
findings.description: The `never` exhaustiveness check in `isSelected`, the ordering of the guide check before the state write, and the lazy fact-gathering are all reasonable. Coverage is good. The resolver unit tests cover D4 selection, D9 guide rejection and the read-only file case. The integration tests cover the 13 listed scenarios, and there is a CLI and MCP parity test. The `canChmod` skip is conditional on platform and uid, not a blanket skip. In `ContextIntegrator.ts`, `project.instruction || 'implementation'` duplicates an existing default string, so it should reference a shared constant if one exists. That is minor.
